newsitem.title: UK: Deutsche Bank in record fund compensation deal.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank in record fund compensation deal.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank agreed on Friday to a record compensation package of around 200 million pounds ($333 million) as a result of irregularities in its funds arm Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
"This is the largest compensation payment that there has been under the Financial Services Act," Judy Delaforce of Britain's Investment Management Regulatory Organisation told Reuters.

IMRO announced earlier it had agreed the basis for compensation for investors in three European funds run by Deutsche's fund management arm and Deutsche confirmed speculation as to the enormity of the bill.
"From today's perspective, we expect to pay about 200 million pounds or about 500 million marks," Deutsche Bank spokesman Hellmut Hartmann told Reuters in Frankfurt.
Trading in the funds was suspended in September following the discovery of irregularities in valuations of unlisted securities in some of the unit trusts.

MGAM fund manager Peter Young was sacked by the firm and his activities are under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO). Young has said he not guilty of any criminal activity and is being made a scapegoat for internal failings.

IMRO has yet to deliver its verdict on what went wrong at Deutsche's London-based fund management arm and is widely expected to impose a record fine, possibly in excess of one million pounds ($1.6 million), and other other disciplinary actions when it completes its investigations.
An IMRO spokeswoman told Reuters this would be "some time in the new year".

The affair has already led to high-level casualties at MGAM with a purge in October of senior management, including chief executive Keith Percy and three other directors, after an internal probe revealed "management failings."

The total cost of the affair to Deutsche, which also stepped in with a 180 million pound ($300 million) cash injection to buy out the suspect securities and ensure the funds could resume trading, is now becoming clearer. But the first cash bail-out may not necessarily be written off in its entirety and banking sources said the loss was likely to be around half.

Other costs Deutsche will have to bear will include IMRO's expenses in bringing the case, the bills run up by both IMRO's and Deutsche's accounting and legal advisers and the additional bureaucratic expenses of assessing individual losses and then making payments to a possible total of 90,000 retail investors.

Deutsche's Hartmann said the bank still expected to post a 1996 profit which would be comparable to 1995. Group net profit, under international accounting standards rules, rose to 2.1 billion marks ($1.35 billion) in 1995 from 1.7 billion marks ($1.09 billion) the year before.

Both parties stressed investors would be fully compensated. IMRO said the package, which commentators said had involved extremely delicate and complex negotiations, safeguarded investors' interests and had been concluded very quickly.

Deutsche promised throughout to make good any losses to investors in the Morgan Grenfell European Growth Trust, the Morgan Grenfell Europa Fund and the Morgan Grenfell European Capital Growth Fund, two of which were managed by Young.

All investors in these funds at any time between August 1, 1995 and September 5, 1996 will be considered for compensation, which will be "the difference between the investment return from the fund and the return provided by a specially compiled index of comparable funds", IMRO said.
Morgan Grenfell will also pay interest on the payments.
MGAM chief executive Robert Smith said all investors would be "compensated at least to the level of their original investment, which means no one will lose money as a result of these events."

IMRO said investors did not need to take any action as letters containing a record of their transactions and further details of the compensation would be sent by Morgan Grenfell in January, with payment due to be completed by April of next year.
